prompt: The supplied async document store loses one of two field updates when `saveTitle()` and `saveTags()` start from revision 7 at the same time. Sequential calls are correct. Use the fixture's barriers to force both completion orders, reconstruct each read/modify/write timeline, identify the violated revision/ownership invariant, implement the narrow synchronization or compare-and-swap correction that preserves both updates, and add deterministic regressions for both orders plus a sequential control. Do not solve the race with sleeps or by serializing all document operations globally.

requirements: two deterministic barriers expose both overlapping save orders
sequential title and tag saves are correct
the document revision is the existing optimistic-concurrency boundary
global serialization of unrelated documents is outside scope

falsifiableChecks.assertion: Both overlap schedules are exercised and at least one reproduces the lost update on the starting revision.
The causal explanation identifies how two actors violate the existing revision/ownership invariant.
Both fields survive in both controlled orders after the fix, sequential behavior remains correct, and no arbitrary sleep/global lock is used.

evidence: the timeline distinguishes actors and contested state
the repair enforces the stated invariant at the owning boundary
verification covers alternate interleavings rather than one lucky run
